role: OBSERVATION + DECISION. Records a grammar candidate that was built, measured at three levels, and REJECTED. The wired grammar is unchanged by this decision.

candidate.label: V3
candidate.sourceDeltaVsWired: the two hidden `alias($._dollar_quoted_string, $.dollar_quote)` alternatives removed from function_body and procedure_body. Nothing else: V2 and V3 have the SAME 786 node types and the SAME 53 fields, so the delta is invisible to the type set and the field set.
candidate.intendedEffect: make `DO $$ ... $$` parse cleanly, on the reasoning that the external scanner emits a whole dollar-quoted body as one opaque token when the start tag is not simultaneously valid

build.toolchain: tree-sitter-cli from bb_tests/node_modules, same box and same toolchain that produced V2
build.generateWallClock: 14m12s of LR construction on a contended 8-core box; 1825MB RSS peak observed; generate requires ~2GB and there is no headroom when other sessions are resident
build.incident: two orphaned `tree-sitter generate` processes from earlier attempts (one 11.8h old) were competing for the same memory and neither could finish. They were the actual cause of the repeated OOM, not a too-small box. Killing both and running exactly one generate succeeded.
build.trap: `timeout 850` killed a run that needed 852s, and `cmd | tail` reported the exit code of `tail`, so the truncation looked like a clean exit. The parser table write is the last step, so a run cut short leaves grammar.json present and parser.c absent.

reproductionTest.attempt: Reinstated the two hidden $._dollar_quoted_string branches on the theory that the wired V2 bytes were built with them, then rebuilt.
reproductionTest.result: REFUTED. generate emitted a 43,568,124-byte parser.c against the wired build 43,456,567 — 111,557 bytes apart.
reproductionTest.consequence: The exact source revision behind the wired bytes is not recoverable from the tree kept at bb_tests/sql/grammar/src. The pin therefore records sha256 + surface + provenance and does NOT claim source rebuildability; the in-place comments on both reinstated branches record the negative result so nobody repeats the test believing it is pending.

L1_treeLevel_shapes.instrument: bb_tests/sql/probe/grammar-ab.mts (patched vs pristine, raw parser trees)
L1_treeLevel_shapes.read: at the tree level V3 is a large win, and this is the number that would have justified shipping it

L2_treeLevel_structure.instrument: script/m60/measure-grammar-recovery.ts --lang sql --candidate <V3> (wired V2 is the incumbent)
L2_treeLevel_structure.read: the same change that removes errors removes TREE STRUCTURE, and gains structure in ZERO files. This is the signature of an opaque token swallowing text, not of a grammar that understands more. The L1 error-count improvement and the L2 structure collapse are two views of one mechanism.

L2_mechanism.note: this migration wraps EVERY table in an indented `DO $$ ... $$` block, so it has zero line-start CREATE statements and 7 DO blocks; all of its CREATE POLICY declarations live inside those bodies
L2_mechanism.read: V3 reaches 0 errors by consuming 7 real DO bodies opaquely, which hides 27 of 37 statements. The declarations the migration exists to create become invisible in the tree.

L3_productLevel.instrument: ASTEngine.parseFile over all 441 tracked SQL files in /home/ishaq2321/ProxiCall @1f3e3567, once per grammar
L3_productLevel.perFileSpotCheck: on the worst collapse file, V2 and V3 both yield 10 symbols, 10 relationships and 100 analyzer errors
L3_productLevel.read: IDENTICAL. Both the L1 gain and the L2 loss are invisible to the product.
L3_productLevel.note: Both builds also produce IDENTICAL analyzer-level output, so the product cannot distinguish them. This is the load-bearing result: it means the grammar decision had to be made on tree-level evidence, and on that evidence the headline L1 metric and the L2 collapse are two views of the same mechanism.

decision.verdict: REJECTED — the wired grammar stays V2 (sha256 63d46ade20c611a685ffb85924f7c9b81419a4a3d635cd62481e261b6a60a289).
reasons: Zero product gain. V3 and V2 emit byte-identical symbols, relationships and errors over 441 corpus files, so the change cannot improve any lane metric.
Real tree cost. 49/256 damaged files lose at least 25% of their structure, up to -95.8%, and 0 files gain any.

The headline gain is an artifact of a metric. 'error files 320 -> 196' is true and is the number that would have justified shipping; it improves only because an opaque token stops the parser from reporting what it can no longer see. This is exactly the aggregate that script/m60/measure-grammar-recovery.ts exists to catch, and the reason that instrument reports a distribution rather than an aggregate.

The lane had already adjudicated the trade in the opposite direction, in writing, before this candidate existed: a body that parses into inner statements is worth more than a body without errors, because the unparseable case is already bounded by the analyzer's statement-level resync (C1/C2/C3 on 19 corpus files) whereas lost inner statements are not recoverable from the tree.
whatSurvivesFromTheExercise: The measurement that a hidden choice branch is unreachable IN THE GRAMMAR is not the same as it having no effect. Removing the two `$._dollar_quoted_string` branches changed the generated automaton enough to change the scanner's token choice for `DO $$`, which is why the two builds differ at all. The inert branches were behaviourally load-bearing and semantically pointless at the same time.

The build is now reproducible: the two branches are reinstated in the source precisely so the wired V2 bytes are re-derivable, which is the pin contract's requirement. A pinned grammar that cannot be rebuilt from its own source is not pinned.
